abstract: Testicular cancer is the most common malignancy in young men with seminomas comprising almost half of all germ cell tumours. Benign ganglioneuromas are rare tumours derived from the sympathetic nervous system. They usually occur in aldolescents and young adults and are predominantly located in the mediastinum and retroperitoneum. We report a case of a patient with synchronous metastatic testicular seminoma with retroperitoneal lymph node involvement and a benign retroperitoneal ganglioneuroma (RGN) which caused diagnostic and management challenges. The patient had a complete response following combination chemotherapy for his seminoma and subsequently underwent complete resection of his ganglioneuroma.
abstract_ja: 精巣がんは若年男性に最も多い悪性腫瘍であり、セミノーマは胚細胞腫瘍のほぼ半数を占める。良性の神経節腫は交感神経系由来のまれな腫瘍で、通常は思春期や若年成人に生じ、主に縦隔と後腹膜に存在する。本報告では、後腹膜リンパ節転移を伴う同時性転移性精巣セミノーマと、良性の後腹膜神経節腫（RGN）を併存した患者を報告する。RGNにより診断と治療の困難が生じた。併用化学療法によりセミノーマは完全奏効し、その後神経節腫を完全切除した。
